title: Ordinary integral models assemble from supplied stratum models
statement: Let ℓ be prime and E a finite-dimensional normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra which is a normed field. Use the coefficients and inclusion O_E,X→E_X of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] and internal modules of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Let X be a scheme with noetherian underlying space, F an internal E_X-module, and S a finite constructible locally closed stratification of X [def-constructible-stratification]. Suppose that for every immersion i_a:Y_a→X of S, one is supplied with an internal i_a⁻¹O_E,X-module N_a constructible on Y_a and an isomorphism from its ordinary scalar extension along i_a⁻¹(O_E,X→E_X) to i_a⁻¹F. Then there exists a constructible internal O_E,X-module N whose ordinary scalar extension is isomorphic to F. The conclusion does not assert that the specified N_a themselves glue without rescaling.

proof.text: Refine the finite stratification to a finite closed filtration and restrict the supplied integral models to the refined pieces. Extend the open pieces by zero and the closed pieces by direct image. These functors are exact; they preserve constructibility by using the supplied stratifications on the support and zero on its complement. Their coefficient-localization comparisons follow from exact filtered localization and the closed-direct-image filtered-colimit comparison. Thus the associated degree-zero rational pieces have integral bounded constructible models.

Each short exact open--closed localization sequence gives a distinguished triangle. The integral scalar-extension essential image is triangulated, so induction over the finite filtration gives an integral bounded constructible complex K whose rationalization is F[0]. This is the denominator-clearing argument encoded in the existing image-closure theorem; it does not assume essential surjectivity. If there are no pieces the scheme is empty and use zero.

Take the degree-zero homology N of K. Bounded constructibility says N is constructible. Exactness of ordinary coefficient localization identifies the degree-zero homology of its derived extension with the ordinary extension of N. Taking degree-zero homology of the isomorphism with F[0] gives the required ordinary scalar-extension isomorphism. No particular preselected lattice on a stratum is required to glue unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem continuousConstructible_integral_gluing (X : Scheme.{u})
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
    (F : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X))
    (S : Scheme.Stratification X)
    (hmodels : ∀ a : Fin S.n,
      ∃ N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (S.domain a)) Ab.{u + 1})
          ((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (S.immersion a)).obj
            (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X)),
        ProEtale.IsConstructibleModuleObject
          ((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (S.immersion a)).obj
            (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X)) N ∧
        Nonempty ((Mod.extendScalars
          ((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (S.immersion a)).map
            (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X))).obj N ≅
          ((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (S.immersion a)).mapMod
            (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X)).obj F)) :
    ∃ N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
        (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X),
      ProEtale.IsConstructibleModuleObject (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) N ∧
      Nonempty ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).obj N ≅ F)
